_source: gcrip/data/ww_world_actors.json - a reference table of Wind Waker world actors that the remake places as inert scenery but that actually DO something in the original game. Mined by reading the zeldaret/tww decompilation at Z:/memRip/sources/tww (read-only) against the ripped placement records in out/rip/GZLE01/godot/stage_data.json. Every claim carries a `file:line` that was actually read, or a real ripped-data path. STRUCTURE: `_ranking` lists the unwrapped actors by placement count so you can see what was skipped; `_conventions` holds the decoding rules that apply to every entry; `_unrecoverable` lists what could not be determined; `actors` is a dict keyed by the PLACED name (the ACTR/SCOB/TGOB name in the .dzs, which is what stage_data.json records). Each actor entry has: name, file (path relative to Z:/memRip/sources/tww), profile (the fpcNm_* from the OBJNAME table in src/d/d_stage.cpp), aliases (other placed names that run the same code, if any), stub (false = the C++ body is real, "partial" = some functions are /* Nonmatching */, true = the body is a generated stub and nothing is minable), placements (count + top stages, read from stage_data.json), params (a decode table: field -> {bits, meaning, proof}), rot_scale (how the placement rot and scale fields are consumed - several actors use rot.x/rot.z as EXTRA PARAMETER WORDS, not as rotations), behaviour, activates_on, effect, implementation_note, confidence, sources.

_conventions.PrmAbstract: Most modern actors decode params with `daObj::PrmAbstract(this, PRM_X_W, PRM_X_S)`, which is exactly `(params >> S) & ((1 << W) - 1)` (include/d/d_a_obj.h:10-17). The PRM_*_W / PRM_*_S enums live in the actor's header. Older actors decode inline with explicit shifts and masks; those are quoted verbatim in the entries.
_conventions.OBJNAME_argument_is_NOT_params: src/d/d_stage.cpp's OBJNAME table has a third column that dStage_actorCreate copies into `fopAcM_prm_class::argument` (d_stage.cpp:1298-1310), NOT into params. Actors that key off a numeric subtype (tsubo, movebox, swpush, cc, stone2, ...) read that subtype out of their PARAMS instead, and the OBJNAME argument only exists so dStage_getName can turn a (profile, subtype) pair back into a name. In every case checked against the rip, the params subtype and the placed name agree - but it is a level-design convention, not something the engine enforces.
_conventions.switch_numbers: fopAcM_isSwitch / onSwitch / offSwitch / revSwitch(actor, n) read and write the save's switch bits, resolved against the actor's HOME room. 0xFF (and -1) mean 'no switch' and are a no-op. This is the same 256-bit space the remake already uses.
_conventions.collision_templates: A `static const dCcD_Src*` block at the top of a .cpp is often a PLACEHOLDER that create() resizes at runtime. Entries below say explicitly when a quoted radius is a real runtime value and when it is a template that could not be verified because the resize sits inside a /* Nonmatching */ stub.
_conventions.scale_bytes: The exporter's `scale` field is already actor->scale, i.e. the placement's raw byte times 0.1 (src/f_op/f_op_actor.cpp:278). Actors that use scale as data (HyoiKam, swpush) multiply it further; see the entries.
_conventions.already_known: Not re-derived here: TagEv params (d_a_tag_event.cpp:18-45), AttTag/AttTagB (d_a_tag_attention.h:55-72), a chest's item id in the high byte of rot.z, and the shared event-bit/register array (d_save.cpp:1201-1210).

_unrecoverable: bable (fpcNm_BL_e, 105 placements) - every one of the 29 functions in src/d/actor/d_a_bl.cpp is a /* Nonmatching */ stub and include/d/actor/d_a_bl.h has an empty class. No param layout, no HP, no speeds. Only the resource/function NAMES survive.

MKanok2 (fpcNm_Obj_Kanoke_e, 93 placements) - include/d/actor/d_a_obj_kanoke.h:8-10 declares `enum Prm_e { }` with an EMPTY body, and all 24 functions are stubs. Five param fields are known BY NAME (type, search, yure, swNo, swNo2) but not by bit position.

Hfbot1C (fpcNm_Obj_Swflat_e, 12 placements) - all functions Nonmatching; the three getters prmGetSwNo / prmGetSwNo2 / prmGetType exist as empty bodies, so the fields exist but their widths and shifts do not.
Sitem (fpcNm_SITEM_e, 38 placements) - a fully generated dtk shell, 16/16 functions Nonmatching, header class has no members. Even what the actor IS is inference from function names.
Aygr (fpcNm_Obj_Aygr_e, 28 placements) - all 9 functions Nonmatching. `prm_get_mdl()` proves params pick a model but not which bits.
s_turu collision radius - the 15.0f body cylinder sits inside daSsk_Create, which is marked /* Nonmatching */ even though the surrounding body is written out. Treat as probable, not certain.
Ktarur / Kbota / Hfbot1C / MKanok2 static dCcD_Src radii - flagged individually in each entry; the barrel one IS overridden at runtime and the template value (r 50 / h 100) is wrong.

Not attempted at all (frequent but lower gameplay value): Figure (135), MKoppu (58), Fdai (58), Bdkobj (56), Otana (43), MOsara (40), Paper (40), RopeR (38), bbaba (37, an enemy that belongs in enemies.json), Fmastr2, Homen2, Htoge1, magtail, pow, gmos, Rdead1, amos, kani, Tpost, MPot, Ksaku, Ikada, Lamp, nezuana, Oqw, Ikori, Search, nezumi, OtbleL, Mkdan1, Shmrgrd, jbaba, ho.

RECOVERED DESPITE BEING STUBS - three actors whose C++ is entirely /* Nonmatching */ were decoded anyway by disassembling their compiled .rel out of the user's own ISO and matching it against config/GZLE01/rels/<name>/symbols.txt: Ysdls00 (d_a_warpls, confidence high - every field cross-checked against all 65 placements), Hcbh (d_a_obj_hcbh, medium) and Sss (d_a_sss, medium). Their `proof` strings cite .text offsets in the .rel, NOT decomp line numbers - a different and weaker class of evidence than the rest of this file, so they carry an explicit `evidence_note`.

Still open on actors that ARE mined: bridge's params bits 8-15 (m02D9) have no established role; s_turu's exact body-cylinder radius; Hcbh's and MKanok2's collision capsule sizes; whether Aygr's model bit is bit 0.

Odokuro.name: Odokuro
Odokuro.placements: Odokuro 346 (M_Dai 123, sea 51, PShip 24, SubD45 24, kaze 23, M_NewD2 17); the same actor also covers Ktaru 270, Ostool 58, Kmtub 58, Kmi02 46, Ptubo 12 on top of the already-wrapped kotubo 654 / ootubo1 594

type.meaning: index into Act_c::M_arcname[16] and Act_c::M_data[16]; picks model, gravity, throw arc, collision size and break effect. Verified against every tsubo placement in the rip: kotubo=0, ootubo1=1, Kmtub=2, Ktaru=3, Ostool=4, Odokuro=5, Kmi02=13, Ptubo=14 - one nibble value per placed name with no exceptions.

itemNo.meaning: what the pot drops when it breaks. 0x3F = nothing. 0x20..0x3E = index (itemNo-0x20) into the game's random drop tables; sub-indices 1..4 are auto-picked from Link's remaining life and 0x0B..0x14 spawn a whole 16-entry burst. Anything else is a literal dItemNo_*.

spec.meaning: special contents. 0x3F = plain pot. 0 = the pot is HIDDEN until its switch turns on. 1/2/3 = that many Bokoblins (fpcNm_BOKO_e, daBoko_c::Type_BOKO_STICK_e) are created and hide with it. 4 = starts in the appear animation. 5 = if the switch is off, moveBg is forced on.

itemSave.meaning: save-flag (itemBitNo) for the drop so a unique item is only collectable once. 0x7F = do not save.

moveBg.meaning: the pot rides moving BG. The actor force-sets bits 14-15 itself (|= 0xC000) when it lands on non-DA moving ground.

cull.meaning: cull-distance class; cleared to 0 when a Bokoblin is inside so the pot is never culled away.

stick.meaning: only read for type 7 (the spine ball) - keeps the 'stuck' attribute instead of 0.

Odokuro.rot_scale: rot.z is NOT a rotation. prmZ_init() copies home.angle.z into mPrmZ then zeroes home/current/shape angle.z; the low byte mPrmZ & 0xFF is a SWITCH NUMBER (prmZ_get_swSave / is_switch). rot.y is the real facing and is also handed to the dropped item. scale is not read.
Odokuro.behaviour: The universal small carriable prop - pots, barrels, stools, skulls, pails, seed pods. Link lifts it, carries it and throws it; it tumbles, breaks on impact, on a sword hit, or on a fall over 200 units, sinks in water and burns in lava. Odokuro (type 5) is the bone skull used all over the dungeons and the Great Sea platforms; mechanically identical to kotubo, only its numbers, model and break effect differ (eff_break_skull).
Odokuro.activates_on: Link's lift button when in range (attention ACTION_CARRY, range data().mAttnDist), or any attack on its cylinder. A spec==0 pot with its switch off does not exist yet and pops in when the switch turns on (mode_hide -> mode_appear_init).
Odokuro.effect: Drops the itemNo/itemSave item on break; spec 1..3 releases hiding Bokoblins. Sets no flags itself.
Odokuro.implementation_note: THE cheapest big win in the rip. This is the same actor the remake already wraps as res://actors/carriable.gd for kotubo/ootubo1/koisi1/Ktaru - Odokuro (346, the single most common unwrapped actor), Ostool (58), Kmtub (58), Kmi02 (46) and Ptubo (12) are just more rows in that KINDS table. Numbers straight out of M_data[type] as (mGravity, m14 throw-up, m18 throw-forward, mAcchCirRad radius, m70 height, mAttnDist): kotubo[0] -6.0/27/36/30/60/8 - which matches the existing carriable.gd row exactly, so the mapping is verified; Kmtub[2] -6.5/22/43/50/100/11; Ktaru[3] -6.0/27/36/35/70; Ostool[4] -6.0/27/36/40/80/12; Odokuro[5] -6.0/27/36/28/60/8; Kmi02[13] -5.0/25/45/50/100/10; Ptubo[14] -6.5/22/43/50/100/10. Also wire up itemNo/itemSave so pots finally drop something, and rot.z's switch byte.

Ospbox.name: Ospbox
Ospbox.placements: 160 (Asoko 70, SubD44 49, SubD51 22, H_test 8, K_Test5 4, Obombh 4, Atorizk 3)

itemNo.meaning: drop, passed to fopAcM_createItemFromTable with itemBitNo hard-coded to 0x7F (never saved). 0x3F = nothing, which is what 145 of the 160 placements carry.

spec.meaning: index into a static 8-entry profile table. 1, 2 and 3 spawn a PIG (fpcNm_KB_e, which OBJNAME maps to the placed name "Pig", d_stage.cpp:798) with parameter 0x01FF0000 / 0x01FF0001 / 0x01FF0002 instead of dropping an item. 0 and 4..7 fall through to the item drop. Observed in the rip: 7 (x145), 3, 1, 2, 0.

unused.meaning: never read - the header declares only these two fields.

Ospbox.rot_scale: shape_angle builds the model matrix and scale multiplies the model (init_mtx), but neither is decoded into gameplay data. 157 of 160 placements are rot (0,0,0).
Ospbox.behaviour: A stone crate that stands as solid MoveBG world collision (its own Ospbox.dzb) and can ONLY be destroyed by a bomb - its Tg mask is exactly AT_TYPE_BOMB and nothing else. Two frames after spawn it locks its BG. When a bomb hits it, it makes its item (or its pig), plays the break particle and sound, and deletes itself.
Ospbox.activates_on: a bomb explosion overlapping its cylinder.
Ospbox.effect: deletes itself (removing the wall) and either drops an item or spawns a pig. Sets no switch, orders no event.
Ospbox.implementation_note: The collision numbers here ARE real: Create() does mCyl.Set(M_cyl_src) with no runtime resize, so radius 75 / height 150 centred on the origin is correct, and the cull box is -76..76 XZ, -1..151 Y. Godot: a StaticBody3D with the baked Ospbox mesh, an Area3D cylinder r=75 h=150 that only listens for bombs, and on hit free the body and spawn the item or pig.

s_turu.name: s_turu

mode.meaning: 0xFF = permanently grown and hazardous from room load (collision armed immediately, scale 1). 1 = grows when the player is inside the trigger radius and RETRACTS again once he is more than radius+100 away. 0 (and anything else) = grows on approach and then stays grown.

radius10.meaning: trigger radius divided by 10. 0xFF is normalised to 0, and 0 means the default 400.0f. The retract distance is that radius + 100.0f.

swSave.meaning: switch number, 0xFF = none. If the switch is ALREADY on when the room loads, the actor refuses to create (cPhs_ERROR_e). If it turns on later the plant shrinks away and deletes itself.

bits_16_23.meaning: not read anywhere in the file.
bits_16_23.proof: src/d/actor/d_a_ssk.cpp:371-373 - the only three param reads in the translation unit

s_turu.rot_scale: rot.y is the facing used for the model matrix. scale is NOT placement data - the actor drives it itself (0 while hidden, lerped to 1 as it grows) and every placement in the rip is 1,1,1.
s_turu.behaviour: The obstructive thorn plant (its sounds are JA_SE_OBJ_JAMA_SHOKU_IN/_OUT, 'obstruction plant'). It lies dormant at zero scale, then a burst of rock and smoke plays and it grows to full size; once grown it sways on a per-joint sine (5 joints, periods 2000/1300/1000 with 20000/12000/15000 phase offsets, amplitudes 2000/2000/4000 in angle units) and its cylinder becomes an AT collider (AT_TYPE_UNK2000, power 1) that hurts Link on contact. The boomerang cannot hit it; most other weapons can.
s_turu.effect: damages Link on contact while grown. Sets nothing; it is a pure obstacle whose existence is gated by swSave.
s_turu.implementation_note: Body cylinder radius 15 / height 0 comes from the static body_co_cyl inside daSsk_Create, and daSsk_Create IS marked /* Nonmatching */ (d_a_ssk.cpp:333) even though the surrounding body is written out and calls mCyl.Set(body_co_cyl) with no resize - so treat r=15 as probable, not certain. Godot: an Area3D that arms and disarms with a grow tween (cLib_addCalc2 toward 1.0, rate 0.5, max step 0.3; shrink with cLib_addCalc0 rate 0.5 / step 0.3, scale.y leading x and z) plus a sine sway on the visual.

Ocanon.name: Ocanon
Ocanon.placements: 139, of which 138 are in `sea` (the rest is one test-stage copy)

scaleStep.meaning: 0xFF = leave scale alone; otherwise scale is set uniformly to 1.0 + n*0.1. Every placement in the rip uses 0x05, i.e. scale 1.5.

swAppear.meaning: 'appear' switch, 0xFF = none. If set and the switch is OFF at create, the cannon starts in mode 3 (modeSwWait) with its map marker cleared, and only appears (mode 4) once the switch turns on.

pathId.meaning: dPath room-path index. In the retail build 0xFF makes _create fail outright, so EVERY live Ocanon has a path - and the path is used as a REGION, not a route: modeWait only fires when the player is inside it (dNpc_PathRun_c::chkInside). The path polygon is the cannon's firing zone.

swDead.meaning: 'destroyed' switch, 0xFF = none. If already ON at create the cannon starts in mode 2 (already blown up); when destroyed, modeDeleteInit turns it ON.

Ocanon.rot_scale: shape_angle drives both the model matrix and the barrel aim (setMtx / lockonCannon work off shape_angle.y and shape_angle.x). Placement scale is overwritten from scaleStep whenever that is not 0xFF.
Ocanon.behaviour: The wall-mounted enemy cannon of the Great Sea (archive "WallBom", joint WALLBOM_JNT_SHOT). It sits still, tracks the player and lobs a bomb whenever he is inside its path region. It leads the target: aim point = the player's position pushed 150 units back along his facing, plus (distance - 2000) * 0.2 more when he is far, plus a flat 3000 while Link is swimming, plus 200*(6 - shots the boat has fired) as a deliberate miss-bias on the first six shots. 2 HP.
Ocanon.activates_on: the player entering the dPath region while the 30-frame reload timer has expired.
Ocanon.effect: creates a daBomb actor with 22 frames of no gravity. When destroyed it sets swDead, sprays four particle effects and clears its map marker.
Ocanon.implementation_note: Real numbers from the HIO defaults: lead 150, far-aim threshold 2000 with 0.2 gain, swim bonus 3000, reload 30 frames, aim turn 0x3000, bomb no-gravity 22 frames, health 2. Collision: mSph.Set(m_sph_src) with radius 75 and NO runtime resize, so 75 is real. Cull box (-100,-100,-10)..(100,100,150) times scale.x. Implementing this one actor populates the Great Sea with its main hazard.

door10.name: door10
door10.placements: door10 159 (TF_06 32, GanonJ 21, ma2room 17, ma3room 17, Siren 15, M_NewD2 12) + door20 13 (one per boss room)

swbit.meaning: front-side switch / save-flag index, 0xFF = none. Used three ways depending on type: the lock flag for a key door (if !isSwitch(swbit) the padlock model shows and the door is locked; unlocking calls onSwitch(swbit)), the switch that raises the front stop-bars, or the switch that gets SET when the room is cleared.

type.meaning: 0 = plain switch/bar door (door10.bdl). 1 = BOSS DOOR: boss-key lock, door20.bdl, attention point +250, drawn with map mode 1 - and every door20 placement in the rip carries type 1. 2 = front-side 'enemy clear' door that opens itself once the front room has no enemies and then SETS swbit. 3 = the small door11.bdl (also uses a much narrower approach box, 15^2 instead of 110^2). 4 and 5 = small-key locked; 5 additionally does the enemy-clear auto-open on the BACK side.

eventNo.meaning: event-manager event number; feeds dComIfGp_evmng_getToolId(eventNo, i) for i=0..11, selecting the 12 cutscene variants (STOP_OPEN / SHUTTER_DOOR_F / SHUTTER_DOOR_F_STOP / BS_SHUTTER_F / KNOB_* / HKYO_DOOR / SHUTTER_DROP_CARRY). door10 passes spl=1 so slots 2 and 3 become DEFAULT_SHUTTER_DOOR_10.

swbit2.meaning: BACK-side stop-bar switch, 0xFF = none. A non-0xFF value is also what makes the stop-bar model get created at all.

bits_28_31.meaning: unused by door10 - only knob00 reads this range.
bits_28_31.proof: src/d/actor/d_a_door10.cpp - no read of >>0x1c anywhere in the file

door10.rot_scale: rot.x packs BOTH room numbers: frontRoom = rot.x & 0x3F, backRoom = (rot.x >> 6) & 0x3F, 0x3F meaning none. The actor's own room is set from frontRoom and the dBgW is tagged with it; opening does dComIfGp_roomControl_offStatusFlag(toRoom, 0x08) and closing re-ons the fromRoom flag - that IS the room streaming handoff. rot.y is the facing yaw, turned into the front normal (sin y, 0, cos y). rot.z is two fields: shipId = rot.z & 0x3F (if != 0x3F, dStage_setShipPos repositions Link's boat on the far side) and arg1 = (rot.z >> 8) & 0xFF. arg1 values door10 acts on: 1..4 enable the Hkyo 'sealed' overlay; 13 and 14 swap in the DoorBs archive models; 15 skips the 65-frame enemy recheck; 16 with type 1 allows the back-side open; 17 makes the bars use the CAGE_OPEN/CLOSE SE. Scale is not read.
door10.behaviour: The classic vertically-sliding dungeon shutter. It is a MOVE_BG collision wall; when Link approaches from the correct side and faces it he gets a door prompt, then it rises 300 units while he is walked through, and slams back down behind him. Optional extras: a small-key or boss-key padlock (dDoor_key2_c), steel stop-bars in front (dDoor_stop_c, model stop10 from the STAGE archive), and a glowing Hkyo seal.
door10.activates_on: proximity plus facing: checkArea(getSize2X(), 110^2, 250^2) - Link within 250 units in XZ, inside a narrow box in front, facing within ~0x5000 of the door normal - then dEvtCnd_CANDOOR_e lets A start the door event. A key lock suppresses the offer unless getKeyNum() != 0 or isDungeonItemBossKey(). Stop-bars raise when their switch turns on, or (type 2 front / type 5 back) automatically 65 frames after fopAcM_myRoomSearchEnemy(room) returns NULL.
door10.effect: consumes one small key and permanently sets swbit for a locked door; hands the player to the adjacent room via the roomControl 0x08 flag swap (plus dStage_setShipPos if a shipId is set); sets the restart/respawn point 180 units on the far side; a type 2/5 door SETS swbit when the room is cleared.
door10.implementation_note: Godot: an AnimatableBody3D wall plus a trigger area. Decode swbit/type/eventNo/swbit2 from params and frontRoom/backRoom from rot.x, arg1/shipId from rot.z. Gate the prompt on the checkArea test (distance 250, in-front box, facing within ~112 degrees) AND on key possession. On open, disable the collider and tween the mesh +300 on Y (open speed ramps 0->30 at +4/frame, close ramps to 60 at +6/frame), walk Link forward, then reverse; set the respawn point on close. Model: type 1 -> door20, type 3 -> door11, else door10, unless arg1 is 13/14. The stop-bars are a separate stop10 model that slides 0->300 on Y independently, driven purely by switch/room-cleared state. Do not hardcode the collision box - it comes from the per-type .dzb in the stage archive.

door12.name: door12

swbit.meaning: front-side switch / lock flag, 0xFF = none. Same triple duty as door10.

type.meaning: 0 = plain switch/bar door. 1 = SMALL-KEY locked. 2 = front-side enemy-clear auto-open. 3 = BOSS DOOR (boss key, map mode 1, forces event slot 6 DEFAULT_BS_SHUTTER_F). NOTE type is writable: create() calls setType(3) when arg1 is 9 or 12, so those shapes are always boss doors regardless of the authored value.

eventNo.meaning: event number; same 12-slot table as door10 but with spl=2, so slots 2 and 3 become DEFAULT_SHUTTER_DOOR_12.

swbit2.meaning: back-side stop-bar switch, 0xFF = none; also the trigger for creating the stop-bar model.

door12.rot_scale: same base layout as door10: rot.x = frontRoom(bits 0-5) | backRoom(bits 6-11), rot.y = facing yaw, rot.z = shipId(bits 0-5) plus arg1 = (rot.z >> 8) & 0xFF. For door12 arg1 is the MODEL SELECTOR: getShapeType() maps 8->1, 9->2, 10->3, 11->4, 12->5, anything else ->0. Shapes 0/1/2 load the door12 archive, 3/4/5 load door13, and the left/right BDL tables are deliberately swapped for 3-5 (a mirrored hinge). Open width also comes from shape: 140 for 3/4, 220 for 5, 200 otherwise. Extra arg1 effects: 9 or 12 force type 3; 8 clears temp flag UNK_0440 at create and SETS it when the bars finish closing (a scripted cage); 8 and 0xB suppress the door SE when the player is not the trigger; 17 switches the bars to the cage SE.
door12.behaviour: The double door: two half-models slide apart sideways (each half translates +/- progress*openWide along local X) instead of a shutter sliding up. Otherwise it is the same dDoor_info_c machine as door10 - stop-bars, small/boss key, room handoff, restart point.
door12.activates_on: proximity plus facing: checkArea(110^2, 110^2, 250^2), then A. Suppressed while locked unless the key is held. Stop-bars raise on their switch, or (type 2, front only) once the front room has been enemy-free for 65 frames. Special case: if Link is CARRYING something and the shape is 1/2/4/5, event slot 0xB SHUTTER_DROP_CARRY runs instead - the drop-what-you-hold variant.
door12.effect: room transition (roomControl 0x08 handoff plus optional dStage_setShipPos), consumes a small key and sets swbit when unlocking, sets the restart room on close. arg1==8 additionally sets temp flag UNK_0440 once its bars have closed.
door12.implementation_note: Two mesh halves parented to the door origin, translating +/-(progress * openWide) along local X; progress ramps with speed 0->20 at +2/frame both ways, much softer than door10's shutter. openWide is 140/200/220 by shape. Pick the archive by shape (door12 for 0-2, door13 for 3-5) and remember the L/R model swap for 3-5. Collision comes from the archive dzb (DOOR12_G for shapes 0,3,4; DOOR12_B for 2,5). Reuse door10's room-transition and restart-point path - it is the shared base class.

KNOB00.name: KNOB00
KNOB00.placements: KNOB00 75 + KNOB00D 49 = 124 (sea 26, ma2room/ma3room/majroom 30, Pfigure 7, plus most town interiors)

swbit.meaning: inherited dDoor_info_c switch field. knob00 never gates on it itself - it creates no stop-bars and no key lock.
swbit.proof: src/d/d_door.cpp:16-18; include/d/actor/d_a_knob00.h:69 (mStopBars declared but dDoor_stop_c::create is never called in d_a_knob00.cpp)

type.meaning: copied into mDoorType at CreateInit. 0 = plain knob door, just opens. 1 = ALWAYS shows a message first. 2 = shows the message only AT NIGHT. 3 = only during the DAY. 4 = PASSWORD door: on first entry, if event flag UNK_1910 is unset it runs the password-entry flow; once set (and the Bomb Bag is held) the door goes inert.

eventNo.meaning: event number into the 12-slot table; knob00 uses slots 7 (KNOB_DOOR_F_OPEN), 8 (KNOB_DOOR_B_OPEN) and 9 (KNOB_TALK).

shapeType.meaning: picks the door leaf model out of the knob archive: 1->DOOR_B, 2->DOOR_C, 3->DOOR_D, 4->DOOR_E, 5->DOOR_F, 6->DOOR_G, 7->DOOR_H, anything else->DOOR_A. Side effects: shape 1 forces the door off the dungeon map; shape 4 with type 1 promotes mDoorType to 5 (the villa door, which spawns a fpcNm_TAG_MK_e actor with param 0xffffff03 and raises the attention point +60); shape 5 lights the leaf as an actor instead of BG0; shape 6 promotes mDoorType to 6 (the figurine-gallery door, which overwrites home.angle.z with message id 0x366A and talks to the 'Mt' NPC).

type2.meaning: 1 = the door is mounted on a MOVING parent: every frame execute() re-runs calcMtx() and mpBgW->Move() so the door and its collision follow current.pos/current.angle. draw() also checks the parent: if it is fpcNm_Obj_Pirateship_e and its m2CC is 0 the door is not drawn. This is the pirate ship's door.

KNOB00.rot_scale: rot.x is the standard packed room pair (frontRoom bits 0-5, backRoom bits 6-11) but knob00 only forces its own room from it when the placement left roomNo == -1. rot.y is the facing yaw - note calcMtx uses current.angle.y, not home.angle.y, because the door can be carried by a moving parent. rot.z is DIFFERENT from door10/door12: knob00 never reads arg1 or shipId; it uses the whole s16 rot.z as a MESSAGE ID passed to dDoor_msg_c::init. chkException() refuses specific message ids unless story flags line up: 0x6A6 (blocked if the Nayru pearl is held or if UNK_2110 is unset), 0x6A7 (needs UNK_0520), 0x6A8 (needs ENDLESS_NIGHT and NOT UNK_2110), 0x6A9 (blocked by UNK_1701), 0x6AA (needs the Din symbol and NOT UNK_1A80). A shape-6 door has rot.z force-overwritten to 0x366A. Scale IS used - the leaf model gets setBaseScale(scale).
KNOB00.behaviour: The ordinary hinged/knob door of towns and houses (the file's own comment: 'Object - Regular doors (with knobs, not sliding)'). It is one BCK animation - Link turns the knob, the door swings, he steps through and it shuts - rather than a physically animated slab; the leaf mesh is parented to the DoorDummy joint of the animated frame model. Four animation variants (DOOROPENADOOR / DOOROPENBDOOR / the same two started at frame 34) are selected by cutscene action index 0xC..0xF, and 0xC/0xD additionally fade the screen to white (night) or black (day) at frame 15 - that is the town-house interior transition.
KNOB00.activates_on: proximity plus facing, then A: checkArea(80^2, 110^2, 250^2) - a slightly tighter side box than the shutter doors. Slot 7 front, slot 8 back, slot 9 KNOB_TALK for talk/villa/figurine states. A message door (type 1, or 2 at night, or 3 by day) plays the rot.z message first unless chkException() forbids it. The password door opens the software keyboard and compares against fopMsgM_passwordGet.
KNOB00.effect: room transition through the shared base with ship=0, so a knob door NEVER repositions the boat; restart point set on close. Story flags it can set: UNK_1910 on a correct password, UNK_3B20 plus a random 0..5 into event register UNK_BA0F when the password is generated.
KNOB00.implementation_note: Animation-driven, not transform-driven: play a ~70-frame door-open clip on the frame model and parent the leaf mesh to the DoorDummy bone; Link's movement during it is entirely scripted (SETSTART places him at fixed offsets, ADJUSTMENT lerps him to 70 units in front). Decode shapeType from bits 20-27 to pick door_a..door_h, type from bits 8-11 for the message gating, and treat rot.z as a MESSAGE ID, not as arg1/shipId - getting that wrong is the easy mistake here. Honour type2 by re-syncing transform and collision every frame for ship-mounted doors. The white/black cross-fade at 15/70 of the clip is what sells an interior transition. Only one collision shape exists (KNOB_DZB_DOOR), shared by every shape.

SMBdor.name: SMBdor

swbit.meaning: switch index, 0xFF = none. For type 0 this is the switch that must be ON for the door to unbar; for type 1 this is the switch the door SETS once the room's enemies are dead.

shapeType.meaning: model set, decoded inline with an explicit mask (not via PrmAbstract). 1 = the Gbdoor archive (Ganon's tower double door: V_GBDFU frame / V_GBD_L / V_GBD_R leaves / V_GBDTO bar; hinge offsets -300 / +300, bar pivot 335). Anything else = the Mbdoor archive (Forsaken Fortress: S_MBDFU / S_MBD_L / S_MBD_R / S_MBDTO; hinge offsets -255 / +277, bar pivot 300).

unused.meaning: never read - the only decoders in the file are &0xFF and &0xF00.

SMBdor.rot_scale: NOT a dDoor_info_c - daMbdoor_c derives straight from fopAc_ac_c, so it does not inherit the packed room fields and does NO room transition at all. rot.z carries the TYPE: getType() = home.angle.z & 0x3F. Type 0 = switch door (polls isSwitch(swbit)). Type 1 = clear-the-room door (counts down 30 frames of fopAcM_myRoomSearchEnemy(room)==NULL, then SETS swbit and unbars). Type 2 always starts locked and checkUnlock has NO case for it - a type-2 door can only be opened by a cutscene driving it as a dDemo_actor_c. rot.y is the facing yaw (both goal points are derived from it at local z = -150 and -400). rot.x is not read; there is no room-number field. Scale is not read.
SMBdor.behaviour: A large double door with a drop-bar. The bar rotates about Z down to -0x3F65 to unbar; each leaf rotates about Y by up to -0x1C71 (~-40 degrees) about its own hinge offset, and only the leaf on the side Link approached from swings. Link is physically pushed with it (setPlayerPosAndAngle to a point 80 units to the side and 75 forward of the hinge) so it reads as him shouldering the door open. Both stages are event-driven: MBDOOR_STOP_OPEN for the bar and MBDOOR_OPEN for the leaf.
SMBdor.activates_on: two stages. Unbarring is automatic - actionLockWait polls checkUnlock() and orders MBDOOR_STOP_OPEN by itself with no player input. Pushing it open is player-driven - checkArea() requires local z <= 160, |local x| <= 200 of home.pos, and fopAcM_seenActorAngleY <= 0x2000 (facing within ~45 degrees), then dEvtCnd_CANDOOR_e lets A open it.
SMBdor.effect: NO room transition and no restart point, unlike door10/door12/knob00. It sets swbit for a type 1 door once the room is cleared, releases its dBgW collision when it opens, and shows on the dungeon map.
SMBdor.implementation_note: Four meshes under one node (frame, left leaf, right leaf, bar). Bar: rotate about local Z around a pivot at (barOffset, 231, 0), accelerating +40/frame up to 400 angle-units/frame until -0x3F65. Leaf: rotate about local Y around a pivot at (+/-hingeOffset, 0, 0), accelerating +50/frame up to 250 until -0x1C71; pick the pivot side from which side of the door's local X Link is on. Drive Link's position from the door transform while it swings. The two archives have DIFFERENT hinge offsets (-255/+277 vs -300/+300) and bar pivots (300 vs 335). The unlock condition comes from rot.z & 0x3F, not from params - the easy thing to get wrong. Type 2 doors never open on their own.

ATdoor.name: ATdoor

swbit.meaning: the ONLY field this actor reads. 0xFF = the door is permanently inert and never moves. Otherwise the door MIRRORS the switch: on -> open, off -> closed, rechecked every frame in both directions.

unused.meaning: not read anywhere - no type, no shape, no event, no swbit2. There is exactly one model (ATDOOR_BDL_SDOOR01) and one collision (ATDOOR_DZB_SDOOR01).

ATdoor.rot_scale: rot.y is the closed-position yaw: calcMtx does YrotM(home.angle.y - openAmount), so the door rotates AWAY from its authored angle. rot.x and rot.z are NOT read - no room numbers, no arg1, no ship id, no event id. Scale is not read. The room used for the switch query is the placement room.
ATdoor.behaviour: A one-piece jail/gate door that swings 0x4000 (exactly 90 degrees) about its own origin, purely as a slave to one switch. No cutscene, no key, no message, no room transition, no A prompt beyond its attention point being raised 150 units. It is not something Link opens - it is a gate that a lever, chest or defeated enemy elsewhere opens.
ATdoor.activates_on: the switch turning on; fully reversible - it swings shut when the switch goes off. Link cannot interact with it directly.
ATdoor.effect: rotates its own collision open (mpBgW->Move() each frame of the swing) so the passage becomes walkable, and plays JA_SE_OBJ_TC_JAIL_DOOR_OP once when it starts opening (there is no close SE). It sets no flags.
ATdoor.implementation_note: Trivial: an AnimatableBody3D whose Y rotation is home_yaw - open_amount, where open_amount steps 0x400 per frame (1/16 of the 0x4000 travel, so exactly 16 frames each way). Bind it to a switch signal, move the collider with the mesh each frame, play the SE on the opening edge only, and if swbit == 0xFF spawn it as static geometry.

osiBLK0.name: osiBLK0
osiBLK0.placements: osiBLK0 76 (SubD51 44, I_TestR 13, M_NewD2 12), osiBLK1 24, Ecube 15, Mmrr 12, Kkiba 10, Hbox2 10 - 147 pushable blocks in total

TYPE.meaning: Act_c::Type - selects the M_arcname / M_attr row (model, dzb, gravity, push SE, footprint). Verified against the rip: osiBLK0 = 1 (plain black push block, Osiblk/obm_osihikiblk1, 150 cube, gravity -5.0, rock SE), osiBLK1 = 2 (same but with the statue on top, m68 = 300), Kkiba = 0 (breakable wooden crate, gravity -3.0, wood SE), Hbox2 = 5 (golden breakable crate, gravity -3.0), Mmrr = 0xA (the pushable MIRROR, 300-unit footprint, no model of its own), Ecube = 0xC (mossy black block, lit as background with a real shadow). Every placement of each name carries its own nibble with no exceptions.
TYPE.proof: include/d/actor/d_a_obj_movebox.h:122-137 (Type enum with the actor names in comments), :145-146, :169; src/d/actor/d_a_obj_movebox.cpp:73, :294-307, :341-1004

SWSAVE.meaning: swSave1, dual purpose. If pathId != 0xFF it stores bit 0 of the block's path-point index, i.e. how far it has been pushed, so the position survives a save. If pathId == 0xFF it instead gates whether the block spawns at all, compared against DMY.

ITEMNO.meaning: drop-table index when the box is smashed. ACTIVE only for the breakable types 0 (Kkiba) and 5 (Hbox2); unreachable for the others.

ITEMSAVE.meaning: save bit for that drop, 0x7F = do not save.

DMY.meaning: spawn polarity. Set = the block exists only while swSave1 is ON (and rot.z is forced to 0xFFFF, killing the path and swSave2). Clear = it exists only while swSave1 is OFF.

BUOY.meaning: INVERTED: 0 = also spawn a daObjBuoyflag child (a floating marker parented to the box top at +m68-5), 1 = no buoy. For the mirror type this is what decides whether you get a buoy or the fpcNm_Obj_Mmrr_e mirror child.

osiBLK0.rot_scale: rot.y (home.angle.y) survives and defines the PUSH GRID orientation: the four push directions are home.angle.y + {0x0000, 0x4000, 0x8000, 0xC000} and the block's position is always home.pos rotated by home.angle.y plus integer steps. rot.x and rot.z are NOT rotations - they are extra parameter words. rot.z high byte = swSave2 (bit 1 of the saved path index), rot.z low byte = pathId (a dPath id in the home room); rot.x low byte = evId, consumed only when building the MkieBB child (type 0xB). All three angle fields are zeroed after decode. Placement scale only scales the DRAWN model; the collision footprint and push step come from the per-type Attr_c.
osiBLK0.behaviour: A dBgS_MoveBgActor with a real DZB collision mesh. Pushing or pulling a face registers through dBgW's PushPull callback, which buckets the direction into one of four sides relative to home.angle.y and counts consecutive frames; once a side reaches 4 frames and a 74-unit forward line check finds no wall, the block slides exactly 75.0 units over 20 frames on a cosine ease, tracking its position as integer grid offsets from home.pos. It falls under gravity (-5.0 or -3.0 by type) with 5-point (or 21-point for the 300-wide mirror) ground sampling, and switches to a buoyant floating mode if it lands in water.
osiBLK0.activates_on: Link's push/pull held on one face for 4 frames with no wall within 74 units ahead and the block on ground. The mirror (type 0xA) additionally REQUIRES the heavy push (dBgW::PPLABEL_HEAVY) and rejects the normal one. Kkiba and Hbox2 are also destroyed by a bomb blast on their Tg cylinder (r 75, h 150) or by Link's front-roll crash.
osiBLK0.effect: Writes NO gameplay switch by itself. It only persists its own position: path_save() writes bit 0 of the current path point index into swSave1 and bit 1 into swSave2 (rot.z high byte) each time it comes to rest, and path_init() teleports it back to that point on load. When pathId == 0xFF swSave1 is read-only and just decides whether the block exists. Breakable types additionally spawn their ITEMNO/ITEMSAVE drop and delete themselves.
osiBLK0.implementation_note: Godot: a static body that snaps to a 75-unit lattice anchored at home.pos and rotated by rot.y - 4-frame push charge, then a 20-frame eased 75-unit slide, then re-check ground. Gravity -5 (blocks) or -3 (crates) per frame, drop when unsupported, float when in water. Persist the position by writing 1-2 switch bits (the path index) rather than raw coordinates, and honour the spawn gate (pathId 0xFF and swSave1 != 0xFF -> exists only when the switch equals DMY). NOTE the 75-unit step is HALF the 150-unit box footprint - that is literally what Attr_c.m0C says - and the wall probe reaches mScaleXZ*0.5 + 74 units ahead (224 for the mirror). The mirror is TWO nodes: an invisible 300-unit push body plus a visible daObjMmrr child teleported to it every frame.

Kbota_A.name: Kbota_A
Kbota_A.placements: Kbota_A 48 + Kbota_B 35 = 83, spread thinly over caves, dungeons and sea islands

VERSION.meaning: if >= 1 the actor honours swSave2 packed in rot.z; if 0, swSave2 is forced to 0xFF (disabled).

TYPE.meaning: index into M_attr[4]. 0 = latching (FLAG_STAY_PRESSED | FLAG_OBEY_SAVE - stays down when you step off). 1 = momentary (pops straight back up). 2 = inverted (on while up). 3 = the heavy Hhbot variant that needs the Iron Boots, scale 1.5.

MDL.meaning: selects attr.mModelResIndices[0 or 1]. In the shipped table both entries of every type are identical, so it is a no-op.

SWSAVE.meaning: THE switch this button reads and writes. 0xFF = none.

EVID.meaning: event id resolved once at create. Whenever the button changes state it requests that event, i.e. plays the 'here is the door that just opened' cutscene. If no event with that id exists the request is skipped.

Kbota_A.rot_scale: rot.y orients the button model and the top-plate quad used by the ride test. rot.z is consumed as mPrmZ and then zeroed: its low byte is swSave2 (only when VERSION >= 1), which is a LOCK, not an output - with the type-1 flag the button refuses to pop back up while swSave2 is ON, and it starts pressed if that bit is already set. Placement scale IS real data here: scale.x and scale.z are multiplied by attr.mScale (1.0 for the Kbota types, 1.5 for Hhbot) and then baked into the model, into the DZB collision vertices at create, and into the cull box - so a scaled placement genuinely resizes both the button and its collision.
Kbota_A.behaviour: This is a FLOOR BUTTON you stand on, not a push-block - the file's own header says 'Object - Yellow switch (activated by stepping on it)'. Its RideCallback tests each frame whether a riding actor's XZ lies inside the four-vertex top quad inflated by attr.m40/m44, and sets a riding mode; riding for 6 frames sets the pressed flag. It then runs a four-state machine UPPER -> U_L -> LOWER -> L_U, springing between 1 and 0 (spring 0.9, decay 0.6) and physically lowering the four top DZB vertices each frame for a 35.5-unit travel, so anything standing on it descends with it.
Kbota_A.activates_on: anything standing on the top plate for 6 continuous frames - Link, or a pushed movebox parked on it. Type 0 has no heavy-boots requirement (only type 3 does). It also mirrors external state: FLAG_OBEY_SAVE makes it sink on its own if SWSAVE is set elsewhere and rise if it is cleared.
Kbota_A.effect: writes SWSAVE in the actor's HOME room: on() at the bottom, off() at the top, plus JA_SE_OBJ_FOOT_SW_ON. Because type 0 is FLAG_STAY_PRESSED it does NOT pop up when you step off - it stays down and the switch stays on, only rising if the switch is cleared externally. Type 1 (Kbota_B) is the hold-down variant: it turns SWSAVE off again the moment nothing is on it, which is the classic 'park a block on it or the door shuts'. Both also fire the EVID event on each state change and grab a short 10-frame event lock on first contact - the little hitch you feel when the switch clicks.
Kbota_A.implementation_note: Model Kbota_00 (bdl + dzb). Godot: a plate whose top surface sinks 35.5 units on a spring (target 0/1, k 0.9, damping 0.6); require 6 continuous frames of something standing on the yaw-rotated, scale-scaled top quad; on bottoming out set switch SWSAVE, latching for type 0 and momentary for type 1. Make the collision surface really move so riders descend with it. For Kbota_B make sure a resting block keeps the ride flag alive every frame or the switch will chatter, and if VERSION >= 1 with swSave2 set, treat it as latched down while that bit is on.

MhmrSW0.name: MhmrSW0

SWSAVE.meaning: the switch this post SETS when pounded, and also READS - if it is turned on elsewhere the post sinks by itself, and if turned off it rises again. 0xFF = none.

SWSAVE2.meaning: a second switch that is CLEARED when the post is driven down by an actual Skull Hammer pound, but NOT when it sinks because SWSAVE was set externally. 0xFF = none.

MhmrSW0.rot_scale: no parameter packing in rot at all - the full placement rotation is used as shape_angle and applied with ZXYrotM, and placement scale goes straight to setBaseScale. Note the sink, squash and wobble are applied inside a joint callback on MHMRSW_JNT_HIT rather than to the actor transform, so scaling the actor scales the whole animated post.
MhmrSW0.behaviour: The Skull Hammer pound-post. A MoveBG actor (arc MhmrSW) with a Co cylinder Link can stand on and a Tg cylinder that accepts nearly every attack type. set_damage() only counts a hit that carries AT_TYPE_SKULL_HAMMER and comes from the player, then branches on the cut type: a front swing or jump-cut is a real pound, a side swing only makes it wobble. A pound squashes the post to scaleY 0.2 for 18 frames then springs it back, spawns star/shockwave/smoke particles, and drives it 60 units down on a spring.
MhmrSW0.activates_on: being struck by the Skull Hammer with a front swing or a jump attack. It also sinks or rises on its own to follow SWSAVE if that bit changes elsewhere.
MhmrSW0.effect: at the bottom it sets SWSAVE, and if the descent came from an actual pound it additionally CLEARS SWSAVE2. Rising writes nothing. It is a lockable misc target only while up.
MhmrSW0.implementation_note: 60-unit vertical travel on a spring (k 0.8, damping 0.55); collision cylinder radius 100 with height 112.5 up and 52.5 down - these come from fully decompiled Create / mode_*_init calls, so they are real, not placeholders. Squash to scaleY 0.2 held 18 frames then spring back (k 0.8, damping 0.45); the side-hit wobble is a damped two-axis tilt (spring 0.99, damping 0.18). Gate the pound on the hammer's front or jump swing specifically, and keep the post following SWSAVE in both directions so a remote reset raises it.

Hfbot1C.name: Hfbot1C
Hfbot1C.placements: 12, all in Siren (Tower of the Gods)

swNo.meaning: primary switch. The header declares `void prmGetSwNo() const {}` with an EMPTY body and there is no Prm_e enum in the header; the symbol map proves a daObjSwflat::Act_c::Prm_e exists (PrmAbstract is instantiated on it) but its widths and shifts live only in the unbuilt binary.

type.meaning: variant selector (prmGetType, empty stub). The three placed names Hfbot1A/B/C differ only by OBJNAME argument, so the variant most likely rides in this params field.

Hfbot1C.rot_scale: UNRECOVERABLE - set_mtx and init_mtx are Nonmatching stubs, so whether rot.x/rot.z are repurposed as extra param words (as they are in movebox and swpush) cannot be determined.
Hfbot1C.behaviour: From the file's own header comment: 'Object - Tower of the Gods - Floor switch (requires statues to stay active)' - a flat floor pad that only stays activated while something rests on it. Structurally it is a dBgS_MoveBgActor with a dCcD_Cyl, an Hfbot arc (bdl hfbot1, brk hfbot1 colour animation, dzb hfbot1) and an mDoExt_brkAnm, so the pad glows when active. Everything past that is inference from surviving declarations, not readable code.
Hfbot1C.activates_on: weight resting on the pad - stated by the file comment only; the detection code is a stub.
Hfbot1C.effect: sets/clears its switch and probably a second one; which is written and which is read cannot be determined.
Hfbot1C.implementation_note: Do NOT trust the static template: l_cyl_src declares radius 10 / height 20 but it is non-const and Create(), which is where a resize would live, is a stub - the real trigger volume is gone. For Godot: an Hfbot1 pad with a colour/glow animation that turns a switch on while a statue or Link stands on it and off when the weight leaves; take the actual switch numbers from the room's placement params by observation, and size the trigger to the visible pad.

BFlower.name: BFlower

kind.meaning: initial State_e written straight into mState: 0 = LIVE (bomb bud present), 1 = DEAD (burnt/spent stalk).

switchNo.meaning: save-switch number. At create, if that switch is already ON the flower is forced back to LIVE regardless of `kind`; when a DEAD flower is revived by water it calls onSwitch so the revival persists. NOTE there is no 0xFF 'no switch' guard here - switch 0 is genuinely checked when the field is left at 0.

BFlower.rot_scale: rot.x is a MODE FLAG, not just orientation: `if (current.angle.x == 0) mGrabbable = FALSE; else mGrabbable = TRUE`. Despite the name, mGrabbable==TRUE DISABLES the carry prompt, i.e. a tilted/wall-mounted flower can only be cut, not plucked - and the flag is passed as the 'stick' bool into the spawned Bomb2. rot.y is normal yaw. Scale is real: the stalk uses setBaseScale(scale) and the bomb bud starts at the placement scale and lerps back toward 1.0 at 0.05/frame as it regrows.
BFlower.behaviour: A two-model object (VbakH stalk + VbakM bomb bud). In LIVE it idles, wobbles when Link walks within 50 units, and any real weapon hit or bomb blast on its 30-unit sphere spawns an actual Bomb2 actor at its position while the bud shrinks to zero and regrows over ~20 frames. If Link is close enough to pick it, it hands him a Bomb2 directly. In DEAD it is a bare stalk with a 15-unit sphere plus a 50x10 water-catching cylinder, swaying every 100-200 random frames.
BFlower.activates_on: damage or an explosion on its 30-unit sphere, or Link picking it up. A DEAD one re-activates only on an AT_TYPE_WATER hit to its cylinder.
BFlower.effect: spawns fpcNm_Bomb2_e with prm = start | (stick << 8): Start_UNK0 + true when set off by another bomb, Start_UNK1 + mGrabbable when cut by any other weapon, Start_UNK2 + false when plucked and handed straight to Link. A DEAD flower hit by water plays the recover SE, flips to LIVE, turns its switch on and swaps its sphere back to the big one.
BFlower.implementation_note: No HP, no movement, not an enemy. Collision is set in a fully decompiled CreateInit with no runtime resize, so these numbers are real: water-catch cylinder r=50 h=10 on current.pos; LIVE hit sphere r=30 at local (0,30,0) rotated by the flower's angle; DEAD sphere r=15. Cull box -50..50 XZ, 0..100 Y; lock-on point at local (0,50,0). Regrow lerps the bud scale to 1.0 (rate 0.05, max step 0.1, min 0.05); the proximity wobble triggers at XZ distance < 50 with |dy| < 10. Godot: a {live, dead} state machine with one Area3D sphere that switches between r 30 and r 15, plus a separate r 50 / h 10 area that only listens for water.

c_green.name: c_green
c_green.placements: c_green 93, c_red 85, c_kiiro 46, c_black 32, c_blue 26 - 282 ChuChus in total (kindan 37, I_SubAN 20, Siren 21, Cave10 28, sea 23, ...)

behaviorType.meaning: 0 = ground ChuChu that rises out of the floor. 1 = ceiling ChuChu (shape_angle.x set to -0x8000 so it hangs inverted, then drops with gravity -11 when it wakes). 2 = cutscene ChuChu (gravity 0, position driven by a matrix). 3 = home-tethered wanderer that ignores the player and reuses the switch byte as its drop-item flag. 4 = jar ChuChu that finds an fpcNm_TSUBO_e pot at its exact x/z and hides inside it.

colorType.meaning: 0 = green, 1 = red, 2 = blue, 3 = black, 4 = kiiro/yellow - proven by the switch that sets itemTableIdx from the literal strings "c_green"/"c_red"/"c_blue"/"c_black"/"c_kiiro". Values 10-15 mean 'that colour minus 10, but with the notice range forced to 60000 so it is awake from room load'; the special value 15 additionally makes it die to any non-player actor and forces the colour to red. THE PLACED NAME DOES NOT PICK THE COLOUR - all five OBJNAMEs share subtype 255 and daCC_Create reads the colour purely from params.

noticeRange10.meaning: wake-up radius divided by 10. 0 means 1000.0 for most types and 1200.0 for the ceiling type; otherwise byte * 10.0.

switchNo.meaning: dual purpose. For behaviorType != 3 it is an ENABLE-spawn switch: if != 0xFF the ChuChu starts inert with colliders off and off the map, and wakes 40 frames after the switch goes true. For behaviorType == 3 it is copied into stealItemBitNo, the save-flag attached to the item it drops.

c_green.rot_scale: rot.y = initial facing. rot.z is NOT rotation: m340 = current.angle.z * 10.0f clamped to a minimum of 100.0, then angle.z is zeroed - m340 is the leash radius for behaviorType 3 (it walks back toward its spawn point once it strays past it). rot.x is unused as placement data. Placement scale is IGNORED - the cpp never reads scale or calls setBaseScale.
c_green.behaviour: GREEN is the baseline: it sleeps flat and unhittable until the player comes within the notice range, then rises out of the ground and becomes lock-on-able; thereafter it alternates ~10-25 frames walking upright (speed 2.0) with ~70-85 frames crawling as a flat puddle (speed 1.0), and each time it stands up it attacks instead if the player is within 380 units. Attack: wind-up, 10-frame pause, then a leap at speed 18.0 with speed.y 25.0 and gravity -3.0, its body cylinder switched to an attack collider that a shield can block. RED skips the puddle state entirely and attacks whenever the player is within 380. BLUE is ELECTRIC: its attack collider is permanently live, sparks play every 30-72 frames, and while charged ordinary sword hits are REJECTED outright. BLACK is the Dark ChuChu: every normal weapon is filtered out with a clang, only LIGHT matters - a light beam petrifies it (weight forced immovable) and only the Skull Hammer shatters it; its Tingle hint is literally dItemNo_MIRROR_SHIELD_e. YELLOW is red's aggression plus blue's electricity.
c_green.activates_on: player distance < notice range (default 1000), plus the optional enable switch. Colour codes 10-14 make the range 60000, i.e. awake immediately.
c_green.effect: contact/leap damage: power 1 for green and red, power 2 with the shock splash for blue and yellow, power 2 for black. Drops a generic item ball resolved through the per-colour CharTbl row.
c_green.implementation_note: HP by colour (cc_HP_kind): green 2, red 1, blue 2, black 4, kiiro 1. CAUTION: the static body_co_cyl in daCC_Create is a placeholder (r 15, h 0); the REAL collider is set every frame in daCC_Execute - radius 35.0, height 100.0 standing and 30.0 while flattened as a puddle. Ground-clip capsule 20/30. While flattened its target mask is narrowed to bomb/boomerang/arrow/hookshot/hammer/fire-arrow/ice-arrow/light-arrow/light/grapple only - a sword swing cannot hit a puddle. Speeds 2.0 walk, 1.0 crawl, 18.0 lunge; knockback 60 on a lethal hit, 20 otherwise; gravity -3.0, or -11.0 for the ceiling drop; attack trigger range 380; turn rate 0x400/frame walking, 0x1000 attacking. Black needs a three-state machine (immune -> petrified by light -> shattered by hammer) and has stealItemLeft = 3.

bable.name: bable

Oship.name: Oship

subMode.meaning: how much the ship moves. 0 = stationary (never calls pathMove and always uses the short 30-frame reload). 1 = moves along its path while at range A and range B. 2 = moves along its path in every mode including search/idle.

triforce.meaning: 0xF = always spawn. Otherwise the ship only exists once dComIfGs_isCollectMapTriforce(n+1) is true - these are the guard ships that appear on a Triforce salvage spot after you decode its chart.

randomSalvagePoint.meaning: 0xF = any. Otherwise the ship only exists when dComIfGs_getRandomSalvagePoint() equals this value.

pathId.meaning: dPath room path the ship patrols. 0xFF = no path, so it never moves regardless of subMode.

swSink.meaning: switch turned ON when the ship sinks - and if it is already on at create, the ship is not spawned. Sinking also calls daSalvage_c::onSalvageForOship, i.e. this is how a sunken warship reveals its salvage point.

Oship.rot_scale: rot.x is a SECOND parameter word, not a pitch: swRequired = home.angle.x & 0xFF (the ship is only created if that switch is ON; 0xFF = no requirement) and modelType = (home.angle.x >> 8) & 0xFF (0xFF = the ordinary warship; anything else makes isSpecial() true, which suppresses the Moblin flag child, changes the sinking sequence to the scripted GOLD_SHIP_DELETE event and applies scale 0.75). getArg then zeroes angle.x. rot.y is the initial heading.
Oship.behaviour: The Great Sea warship, 3 HP. It sits or patrols a path, watches the player's distance and switches between four range modes (2500 / 6000 / 12000 units), turns its cannon and lobs bombs at the King of Red Lions. When killed it lists over, settles 1000 units below the water surface and disappears; a normal ship drops an item ball, a 'special' one plays the GOLD_SHIP_DELETE cutscene and sets event bit UNK_3E80.
Oship.activates_on: player distance; there is no switch to wake it, only switches that decide whether it exists.
Oship.effect: sets swSink and opens a salvage point on death; fires bombs at the player.
Oship.implementation_note: HIO defaults give a full port: ranges 2500/6000/12000, reload 30 frames close and 200 far, path speed 20 units/frame, bomb muzzle offset (450,0,0), bomb speed 85 with acceleration -2 and 35 frames of no gravity, bad-aim lead starting at 3500 with a max error of 0x3000, attention offset +900 Y, wave offset +380 Z, health 3, special-ship scale 0.75.

HyoiKam.name: HyoiKam

none.meaning: the actor never calls fopAcM_GetParam anywhere in its 1509 lines, and all 51 placements in the rip carry params 0xFFFFFFFF, consistent with that.

HyoiKam.rot_scale: SCALE IS THE PARAMETER. daNpc_kam_c multiplies its placement scale by 1000 at init: scale.x becomes the XZ radius of the seagull's roaming circle around home.pos and scale.y becomes its half-height (max = home.y + scale.y, min = home.y - scale.y). It circles its home point; when Link puts a Hyoi Pear on his head the actor raycasts from the pear position (head top + 20) looking for a clear straight line to descend along, then the nearest seagull dives, lands on the pear and the player takes direct control - stick steers, R or START releases. Flying out past scale.x, or the release button, hands control back.

bridge.name: bridge

typeBits.meaning: a BITFIELD, not an enum. bit0 changes the plank swing model and raises a distance constant from 200 to 1000; bit1 enables an end-section behaviour whose plank count is clamped by total length and pairs the bridge with a partner actor; bit2 disables neighbour-plank coupling; bit3 changes a per-plank count from 3 to 5 and gates the flame handling. bits 0 and 2 together also scale the plank model by 0.85 instead of 1.0. Observed values in the rip: 0x0A, 0x00, 0x01.

unk8.meaning: stored in m02D9; role not established. Every placement in the rip carries 0xFF or 0x00/0x01.

pathId.meaning: REQUIRED - 0xFF makes create fail. Points [0] and [1] of the dPath are the two ENDS of the bridge: home.pos is set to point 0, the far end to point 1, and yaw/pitch are computed from the delta. Plank count = |delta| / ((47 + (|delta| > 1300 ? 3 : 0)) * 1.5); a bridge needing 50 or more planks refuses to spawn.

bridge.rot_scale: The placement rot is OVERWRITTEN - home.angle.y and home.angle.x are recomputed from the path delta at create, and the placement position is replaced by path point 0. A Godot version must read the stage PATH data, not the actor record, to place a bridge.
bridge.behaviour: The rope-plank bridge: a run of individually simulated planks strung between two path points, which sag and swing under Link's weight and can be set on fire.
bridge.activates_on: Link walking on it (per-plank load), and fire.
bridge.effect: walkable, swinging collision. No switch or event.
bridge.implementation_note: Only 2 of the file's functions are /* Nonmatching */, so the plank physics is readable if you need it, but the important structural fact is that the geometry comes from the path: plank spacing is 70.5 units (47*1.5), or 75 for spans over 1300, built from path point 0 to point 1.

lwood.name: lwood

none.meaning: the actor never reads params. All 106 placements carry 0xFFFFFFFF.
none.proof: src/d/actor/d_a_lwood.cpp:1-200 - no fopAcM_GetParam in the file

lwood.rot_scale: current.angle is used for the model and the collision matrix; scale multiplies both. Nothing is decoded as data.
lwood.behaviour: An ordinary tree. Its point is that it carries SOLID COLLISION: CreateHeap does dBgW_NewSet(Lwood.dzb, dBgW::MOVE_BG_e) and registers it with the BG system, so the trunk is a wall - and that collision lives in the OBJECT archive, not in the stage .dzb. Its leaf joint J_Alwd_ha has a node callback that tilts the crown with the wind: rotation = (|sin(t*300)+1| * 250, wind.x * sin(t*300) * 10, wind.z * cos(t*300) * 10) scaled by a per-tree random 0.8..1.2, with t incrementing once per frame from a random start.
lwood.implementation_note: Cheap, high-value: 106 placements currently exported as inert scenery with no collision at all. Adding the Lwood.dzb hull (or a capsule approximating the trunk) plus the wind sway would fix a lot of walk-through trees. Cull box -600..600 XZ, 0..900 Y.

Oyashi.name: Oyashi

none.meaning: no params read; the actor's only attribute row is a single hard-coded constant M_attr = {0, 0}. All 91 placements carry 0xFFFFFFFF.

Oyashi.rot_scale: current.angle.y is used to rotate the wind vector into local space before the sway is computed; the base transform comes from the model's own matrix.
Oyashi.behaviour: The palm tree of the Great Sea islands. Like lwood it registers a MOVE_BG collision hull from Oyashi.dzb, so the trunk is solid. The whole trunk tilts into the wind via a quaternion slerped 0.25 per frame toward an axis-angle of (up x windDir, windPower * 0x600), and two frond joints wave with an angle chased toward min(windPower * 0x180, 0x100) and a phase advanced by windPower * 0x800 plus random jitter.
Oyashi.implementation_note: Same story as lwood: 91 placements (53 in `sea`) that currently have no collision. _execute is marked /* Nonmatching */ but its body is written out in full and readable; CreateInit is the only genuinely missing piece.

Ikari.name: Ikari

envType.meaning: 0xFF = scale 1.0 and actor-style lighting; 0x01 = scale 1.27 and BG0-style lighting with the actor colour registers copied in. Any other value leaves the placement scale alone.
