Ysdls00.evidence_note: PROVENANCE: all 15 functions in d_a_warpls.cpp are /* Nonmatching */ stubs and the header has no members, so this decode does NOT come from readable C++. It was recovered by decompressing and disassembling files/rels/d_a_warpls.rel out of the user's own USA ISO and matching it against config/GZLE01/rels/d_a_warpls/symbols.txt, then cross-checked against all 65 real Ywarp00 + Ysdls00 placements in out/rip/GZLE01/godot/stage_data.json. The .rel offsets below are real read addresses, not decomp line numbers - treat them as a different class of evidence.
aliases: Ywarp00 (type 0 - already wrapped by the remake)
Ysdls00.placements: Ysdls00 45 (one or two in nearly every Cave, plus M_Dai, kaze, Pfigure); Ywarp00 20 (I_SubAN 12, Siren rooms 7 and 17, ...)

type.meaning: arc/model select and THE ONLY thing that distinguishes Ysdls00 from Ywarp00 - the OBJNAME argument byte is 255 for both. 0 = the Ywarp00 arc (BDL 8, BCK 5, BRK 11 - an animated spinning light shaft); 1 = the Ysdls00 arc (BDL 3, BCK and BRK both -1, i.e. NO animation at all). Confirmed empirically: every Ysdls00 placement is 0x10xxxxxx and every Ywarp00 is 0x00xxxxxx.
type.proof: src/d/d_stage.cpp:906-907; d_a_warpls.rel .text:0x7A0-0x7A8 (lwz 0xb0 / srwi 0x1c / stb 0x2bc) with the m_bdlidx/m_brkidx/m_bckidx tables {8,3}/{11,-1}/{5,-1} at .rodata:0x00/0x04/0x08

swNo.meaning: switch gating whether the light column is lit. 0xFF = no switch = always lit. If already on at create the light spawns fully lit (animations jumped to end-3.0 frames); otherwise it is dark until the switch turns on.

sclsNo.meaning: THE DESTINATION - an index into the stage's SCLS (stage-change list) chunk. The warp fires dLib_setNextStageBySclsNum(sclsNo, current.roomNo). It does NOT use dStage_getWarpTable and does NOT call dComIfGs_setRestartRoom; the destination stage, spawn and room all come out of the SCLS entry.

evId.meaning: event id (0xFF = none) for the ACTIVATION cutscene, resolved with getEventIdx and ordered with fopAcM_orderOtherEventId. All 45 Ysdls00 placements use 0xFF.

Ysdls00.second_event_by_name: A SECOND event index is looked up BY NAME from the stage name and room, not from params: in stage "Siren", room 7 -> "TOWER_WARP_U" and room 17 -> "TOWER_WARP_D"; any other stage -> "DUNGEON_WARP". That named event is what actually plays when Link steps in, and when it ENDS the stage change fires. The .rodata string table contains exactly {Ywarp00, Ysdls00, d_a_warpls.cpp, asserts, TOWER_WARP_U, TOWER_WARP_D, DUNGEON_WARP, Siren} and the placement data agrees - the only two Ywarp00 in Siren are in rooms 7 and 17. A JPA emitter is created ONLY for the two TOWER_WARP cases, so every Ysdls00 (always DUNGEON_WARP) has no emitter and no animation - a plain static model.
Ysdls00.rot_scale: Rotation is completely IGNORED - set_mtx is only setBaseScale(scale) + a translation, with no angle read anywhere. SCALE is load-bearing twice: it scales the model, AND the trigger radius is 112.5 * scale.x. Placements vary scale.y between 0.2 and 1.7 to set the visible column height while leaving scale.x at 1.0. Cull box is fixed at (-250, 0, -250)..(250, 2600, 250).
Ysdls00.behaviour: A vertical light column that returns Link out of a secret cave or sub-dungeon. If its switch is on (or swNo is 0xFF) it is lit from the start; otherwise it lights when the switch flips. Once lit, when the player comes within 112.5*scale.x units horizontally it orders the DUNGEON_WARP event, calls setGoal on its own position so Link walks into it, and on event end warps.
Ysdls00.activates_on: the player coming within 112.5 * scale.x horizontal units while the light is lit and the 'spawned already standing in it' guard has cleared. There is no button press.
Ysdls00.effect: plays the warp cutscene, then changes stage to the SCLS entry named by params bits 8-15 of the CURRENT room.
Ysdls00.implementation_note: The remake already wraps Ywarp00 in res://actors/warp_object.gd - Ysdls00 is the SAME actor with type 1. Branch on (params>>28)&0xF: type 1 loads the Ysdls00 single BDL with no bck/brk and no emitter; type 0 is the animated one. Destination = the stage's SCLS[(params>>8)&0xFF] for the actor's room, NOT a warp table. Trigger = a cylinder of radius 112.5*scale.x, ignore rotation, apply the placement scale to the mesh (scale.y 0.3-1.7 is what makes cave lights short and tower lights tall). Gate visibility on the switch, 0xFF meaning always on, and suppress the trigger for the first frames if Link spawns inside it.

Hmlif.name: Hmlif

swNo.meaning: path-switch number, 0xFF = none. When set the lift uses two-path mode: while the switch is ON it runs dPath_GetNextRoomPath(), when OFF it returns to the base path and heads for point mArg0.

pathId.meaning: room-local path index for dPath_GetRoomPath. 0xFF = no path, and then Create() fails and the actor dies.

speed.meaning: index into m_speed[], CLAMPED to <= 8, so the effective speed is (idx+1) * 1.6666667 units/frame = (idx+1) * 50 units/sec at 30fps, maxing at 15.0/frame.

direction.meaning: 0 = forward along the path, 1 = backward, 2 = random +/-1, anything else = forward.

start.meaning: starting path-point index, clamped to 0 if it is >= the point count. NOTE the `if (v == 0xFF) v = cM_rndF(...)` random-start branch at :204-206 is DEAD CODE - a 5-bit field can never be 0xFF.

type.meaning: arc select: 0 = "Hmlif" (the small glowing platform, BRK only), 1 = "Hyuf1", 2 = "Hyuf2". Types 1 and 2 additionally get an arrow-target sphere. All 20 placements use type 0.

smooth.meaning: 0 = lift_normal_move (accelerate / cruise / decelerate, straight-line lerp to the next point), 1 = lift_smooth_move (turns toward the next point with cLib_addCalcAngleS2 and flies along its facing - a curving flight).

Hmlif.rot_scale: rot.z is NOT a rotation - `home.angle.z & 0xFF` is a SECOND switch number, the 'lit' switch, which drives the BTP texture-pattern frame (0..3) and, for types 1/2, is turned ON when the platform is shot by any arrow. All 20 placements have rot.z == 0, i.e. switch 0. set_mtx uses current.angle (not shape_angle), and in smooth mode current.angle.y is overwritten every frame to face the travel direction; the BG collision is registered with dBgS_MoveBGProc_TypicalRotY so it follows that yaw. scale goes straight to the model.
Hmlif.params_observed: Siren 0x000300ff / 0x00030218 / 0x00030320 / 0x000305ff / 0x00030bff / 0x004301ff; SirenMB 0x000000ff / 0x000001ff; I_SubAN 0x87ffffff (smooth = 1, speed clamped to 15.0); K_Test5 0x0003011a.
Hmlif.behaviour: A floating platform that patrols a stage PATH. It picks a start point, a direction and a speed from params, then either lerps point-to-point with an accelerate/cruise/decelerate cycle or steers smoothly toward each point. Closed paths loop; open paths ping-pong. With swNo set it swaps between its own path and dPath_GetNextRoomPath() depending on that switch.
Hmlif.activates_on: nothing - it is always moving from spawn. swNo re-routes it; the rot.z switch changes its glow.
Hmlif.effect: rideable moving BG (dBgS_MoveBgActor); plays JA_SE_OBJ_FLOAT_LIFT_MOVE whenever it is actually moving, and the BRK colour animation loops only while moving.
Hmlif.implementation_note: This is a PATH FOLLOWER, not a fixed-travel lift - you need the stage PATH/RPAT chunk exposed per room, because the travel distance comes entirely from the path points. Speed = ((params>>16 & 0xF, clamped to 8) + 1) * 50 units/sec. The platform must carry the player. Normal mode: accelerate at rate 1/4 toward the target speed, cruise, then decelerate to speed/2.2 when within 50 units of the next point. Smooth mode: turn toward the next point at up to 0x400/frame and advance when within 80 units. Cull box (-200,-100,-200)..(200,50,200) for type 0.

Mhsg4h.name: Mhsg4h

type.meaning: ladder length and model: 0 = MHSG6 (600 units tall), 1 = MHSG9 (900), 2 = MHSG12 (1200), 3 = MHSG15 (1500), 4 = MHSG4H (450). Each type selects its own BDL and its own DZB collision mesh. Every Mhsg4h placement ends in 0x04, i.e. the 450-unit ladder.

swSave.meaning: the switch that DROPS the ladder. 0xFF, or a switch already on at create, means the ladder starts already down (snapped to the ground, Mode_FELL). Otherwise it waits until fopAcM_isSwitch becomes true.

evId.meaning: event id for the drop cutscene, 0xFF = none. Create resolves it with getEventIdx; Mode_DEMOREQ orders it and waits. If the event does not exist it falls straight through to the shake and drop.

Mhsg4h.params_observed: Abship 0x0001e004 / 0x0004e504 / 0x0005e004 / 0x0005e504 / 0x0008e904 / 0x00ffe404 / 0x00ffe504; PShip + SubD45 + SubD71 0x00ffe004; M_Dai 0x00ff3404; K_Testd 0x00ffff04 (starts already down). So type 4 everywhere, swSave in {0x34, 0xe0, 0xe4, 0xe5, 0xe9, 0xff}, evId in {0x01, 0x04, 0x05, 0x08, 0xff}.
Mhsg4h.rot_scale: shape_angle is used: the ground probe is placed at current.pos rotated by shape_angle.y and offset (0, 10, 5), and set_mtx is transS(current.pos) then ZXYrotM(shape_angle) then a small vibration offset. scale goes to setBaseScale. All 17 placements are scale 1 and rot (0, y, 0).
Mhsg4h.behaviour: A retractable ladder that hangs retracted at its placed position and DROPS to the floor when its switch turns on. Modes: WAIT -> (switch on) DEMOREQ (optionally play the event) -> VIB (15 frames of a cosine wobble, +/-2.0 in X and +/-1.0 in Y) -> DROP (gravity -5.0, falls to the ground height sampled at create, bounces 3 times with speed.y *= -0.5 and a descending set of SE pitches) -> FELL. Both the model and its DZB collision move as one MoveBgActor.
Mhsg4h.activates_on: its switch becoming true. NOT Link pulling it and NOT proximity.
Mhsg4h.effect: plays the ladder-fall SE with the ground material sound plus a rumble on first impact, then a lighter SE on each of the 3 bounces. Once fallen it is a permanent climbable ladder.
Mhsg4h.implementation_note: The climb surface is the archive's DZB mesh for this type (Mhsg.arc, dRes_INDEX_MHSG_DZB_MHSG4H_e) - its polygons carry the climb attribute, so wire it into the existing ladder-climb code rather than inventing a box. Geometry: 450 units tall, roughly x in [-55,55] and z in [-10,10]. Travel is from the placed Y down to the ground raycast at (pos rotated by yaw + (0,10,5)); gravity -5 units/frame^2, 3 bounces at 50% restitution. Do the 15-frame shake first - it is the visual cue. Persist the fallen state via the switch, not a local flag.

Hjump2.name: Hjump2

type.meaning: 0 = Type_SPRING_e (BDL/DZB hjump2, the bare springboard, has a simple shadow, cull height 151). 1 = Type_SPRING_ON_BOX_e (BDL hjump1 / DZB hjump1b, a springboard mounted on a crate 150 units higher, no shadow). ALL 12 placements are params 0x00000000, i.e. type 0; type 1 is only produced from code via prm_make_b().

Hjump2.rot_scale: set_mtx is transS(current.pos) then ZXYrotM(shape_angle), followed by a Y-axis squash matrix about the spring height; init_mtx applies setBaseScale(scale). shape_angle.y also feeds the simple shadow. Placement rot.y is what aims the board (0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees all appear); all placements are scale 1.
Hjump2.behaviour: A spring pad that only works with the IRON BOOTS (the file's own header: 'Object - Wind Temple - Iron Boots springboard'). Its ride callback flags who is standing on it and whether that rider is heavy. In WAIT, any rider adds a small bounce impulse; once a HEAVY rider has stood on it for 15 frames it plays the close SE and compresses to scale 0.1. In LOWER it stays compressed while heavy; once the heavy load is gone for 5 frames it plays the open SE and springs out to scale 1.2, and at the instant it reaches 1.2, if the player is still on it, it calls player->onForceVomitJump().
Hjump2.activates_on: compression: Link standing on it wearing the Iron Boots for ~15 frames. Launch: taking the boots off (or the heavy load leaving) for ~5 frames while Link is still on the pad.
Hjump2.effect: LAUNCH VALUES, taken from the player side because the actor only raises a flag: onForceVomitJump -> daPyFlg1_FORCE_VOMIT_JUMP -> procVomitJump_init(0), which sets speed.y = 64.5 units/frame plus a rumble and the spin animation. In flight shape_angle.x spins +22000 per frame, horizontal speed chases 12.725 * stick magnitude, and gravity is the normal -2.5 units/frame^2 - an apex of roughly 832 units, about 26 frames up.
Hjump2.implementation_note: The spring visual is a Y-scale of joint 1 driven by a damped spring (k 0.7, damping 0.4; targets rest 1.0, compressed 0.1, released 1.2) with the top plate translating 85 units. Gate the compression on the Iron Boots equip flag (checkEquipHeavyBoots), NOT on plain contact. Launch: set vertical velocity to 64.5 units/frame and let normal jump gravity -2.5/frame^2 take over, with ~12.725/frame of horizontal control while airborne. Collision is a MoveBgActor, cull box +/-60 XZ. NOTE Execute() carries a /* Nonmatching */ marker but its body is present and complete - the marker only flags a codegen mismatch.

Hfuck1.name: Hfuck1

none.meaning: the actor never calls fopAcM_GetParam at all, and all 42 placements carry 0xFFFFFFFF. There is nothing to configure per placement - every one in the game is identical.
none.proof: src/d/actor/d_a_obj_hfuck1.cpp (no GetParam/PrmAbstract anywhere in the file); out/rip/GZLE01/godot/stage_data.json

Hfuck1.rot_scale: Both matter. init_mtx is setBaseScale(scale) then transS(current.pos) then XYZrotM(shape_angle) - note XYZ order, not the usual ZXY. The hit sphere is placed in that rotated local frame: translate (0, 0, -50) then SetR(90.0f), i.e. the catchable volume is a 90-radius sphere sitting 50 units out along the plate's local -Z. Placement rot.y steps in 45/90-degree units to face the plate at the player.
Hfuck1.behaviour: A wall-mounted HOOKSHOT TARGET (the decomp's own file comment says exactly that, and the DEMO-build HIO panel is named the Japanese for 'hookshot target'). It registers its DZB as MOVE_BG solid collision and keeps a dCcD_Sph whose only Tg type is AT_TYPE_HOOKSHOT. When a hookshot hits it, it records the hookshot actor and the next frame calls player->setHookshotCarryOffset(its own id, {0,0,0}), telling the hookshot to reel Link to this actor's origin.
Hfuck1.activates_on: the hookshot projectile entering the 90-radius sphere offset 50 units along local -Z. Nothing else can trigger it.
Hfuck1.effect: Link is pulled to the target's position and hangs there. No sound, no animation, no state change on the actor.
Hfuck1.implementation_note: A pure hookshot anchor - 42 of them, and the remake's hookshot has nothing to grab without them. Give it an Area3D sphere r=90 centred at local (0,0,-50) on a hookshot-only layer, plus a static collider from the Hfuck1 DZB so Link does not clip through the plate. On hit, drive Link to the actor origin with zero offset and put him in the hanging state. Honour shape_angle on all three axes in XYZ order and the placement scale - both the mesh and the sphere offset rotate with it.

Hcbh.name: Hcbh
Hcbh.evidence_note: PROVENANCE: all 16 functions are /* Nonmatching */ stubs and the header's four param getters are empty bodies with no widths. The layout below was recovered by disassembling files/rels/d_a_obj_hcbh.rel from the user's own ISO against config/GZLE01/rels/d_a_obj_hcbh/symbols.txt - the generic daObj::PrmAbstract<daObjHcbh_c::Param_e> is present at .text:0x1BB4 and is verbatim (params >> S) & ((1<<W)-1), so the W/S immediates at each call site give the exact layout. Cross-checked against all 51 placements. This is disassembly evidence, not decomp line numbers.
Hcbh.placements: 51 (GanonJ 11, Siren 10, TF_01 8, TF_02 8, KATA_RM 6, Cave10 4, SirenMB 4)

itemNo.meaning: item-table index dropped when the pillar is destroyed; 0x3F = nothing. Passed as argument 2 of fopAcM_createItemFromTable.
itemNo.proof: d_a_obj_hcbh.rel .text:0x910-0x918 (li r4,6 / li r5,0 / bl PrmAbstract), result used at :0x978-0x998

itemSave.meaning: the 'already collected' save bit for that drop; 0x7F = none.

swSave.meaning: save/zone switch, 0xFF = none. Dual role: chk_appear() returns FALSE when the switch is already ON and _create then returns cPhs_ERROR_e, so a pillar you already broke never respawns; and make_item() calls onSwitch(swSave, roomNo) after it breaks.

Hcbh.params_observed: Siren / SirenMB / GanonJ / Cave10 use 0x001fffXX with XX in {c0, ca, cb, cc, ce, d0, d2, e0, ff} - so no item save bit, no switch, itemNo = XX & 0x3F. TF_01 and TF_02 use 0x00117fd0 .. 0x00125fec - itemNo 0x04/0x0c/0x10/0x2c/0x33 and swSave 139..146, which is inside the dungeon-switch range 0x80-0xBF. KATA_RM x6 are 0xffffffff (the all-none default).
Hcbh.rot_scale: shape_angle IS used - set_mtx ends with XYZrotM(shape_angle) before writing the base matrix, and every placement carries a distinct rot.y. Placement scale is 1.0 everywhere and no setBaseScale was found in the recovered create path, so treat scale as unused. The toppling transform layered on top is: translate(pos.x, fallY, pos.z), YrotM(fallDir), translate(0, pivot, 0), XrotM(tilt), translate(0, -pivot, 0), YrotM(-fallDir).
Hcbh.behaviour: NOT a traversal actor - it is a tall stack-of-blocks stone pillar (the decomp file comment calls it 'Tower of the Gods - Pillar with Companion Statue's face on it'). It is built from FIVE models out of Hcbh.arc: HCBH2 as the base plus four HCBH1A/1B/1C/1D segments, each pre-rotated by one of the four fixed Y angles {180, 270, 90, 0} degrees. Overall about 590 units tall with a radius-70 wall cylinder, carrying six damage spheres of radius 35 stacked at local Y = 157, 227, 297, 367, 437, 507. When a break condition fires it computes the fall direction as atan2s away from the attacker, gives each of the four segments its own tumble delay, plays smoke and an impact SE, and topples.
Hcbh.activates_on: exactly four break conditions, decoded from checkCollision / co_hitCallback: AT_TYPE_BOMB -> cause 3; AT_TYPE_SKULL_HAMMER -> cause 2; AT_TYPE_UNK8 from an actor whose profile is fpcNm_TN_e (Darknut) -> cause 1; AT_TYPE_DARKNUT_SWORD -> cause 1; and a Co push hit from an actor whose profile is fpcNm_AM_e (Armos) -> cause 4. Nothing else breaks it.
Hcbh.effect: topples into 4 tumbling blocks, optionally spawns an item, and sets swSave so it stays broken across reloads. Until then it is a solid dBgW obstacle.
Hcbh.implementation_note: Spawn only when swSave is unset. Body = a 590-tall radius-70 cylinder collider, visually 4 stacked segments at Y ~157/227/297/367/437/507 each yawed by one of {180,270,90,0} plus a base. Damage volume = 6 spheres r=35 at those heights. Accept damage only from bombs, the Skull Hammer, a Darknut attack, or an Armos body-check. On break pick the direction away from the attacker, tumble the 4 pieces with staggered delays, spawn the drop, set the switch. Apply the placement rot.y to the whole assembly.

Sss.name: Sss
Sss.evidence_note: PROVENANCE: all 17 functions are /* Nonmatching */ stubs and the header class sss_class has no members. Params and key constants were recovered by disassembling files/RELS.arc/rels/amem/d_a_sss.rel from the user's own ISO against config/GZLE01/rels/d_a_sss/symbols.txt, then cross-checked against all 41 placements. Disassembly evidence, not decomp line numbers.
Sss.identity_correction: Sss is the DEXIVINE ENEMY, not a climbable rope and not a variant of d_a_ss.cpp. The two are sibling implementations by the same author (both have hand_draw / hand_move / hand_main / useHeapInit, both fopAc_ENEMY_e, list 7) but they are different creatures: `Ss` (fpcNm_SS_e, d_stage.cpp:892) loads Ss.arc whose model is 'sw' with joints DODAI/EYE/GAKU/TUBOMI and OPEN/CLOSE/DAMAGE/WAIT anims (a flower-bud plant), while `Sss` loads Sss.arc whose only model is 'sss_hand' with joints UDE (arm), NAKAYUBI (middle finger), YUBI1, YUBI2 and anims sss_hiraku (open) / sss_tojiru (close), plus an mDoExt_3DlineMat_c for the vine. The decomp file comment names it: 'Enemy - Dexivine (Forbidden Woods, Wind Temple)'.

segCount.meaning: vine segment count, but with only two possible outcomes: `v = params & 0xFF; if (v == 0xFF) v = 0; if (v != 1) v = 0x23;` - so 0x01 gives the short 1-segment form and 0x00 or 0xFF give the full 35-segment vine.

range10.meaning: player-detection radius = 10.0 * this value; 0xFF means use the default 250.0. Observed: 0x46 (700), 0xC8 (2000), 0x3C (600), 0x50 (800), 0xFF (250).
range10.proof: d_a_sss.rel .text:0x2AA4-0x2AAC, consumed in hand_move at .text:0x1664-0x1694 against fopAcM_searchActorDistance

swNo.meaning: an alternative switch trigger - if non-zero, isSwitch(swNo, roomNo) also wakes it. When the field ends up 0 (which is every placement) the actor's stored retract-target Y is raised by 10000.0, i.e. effectively infinite. All 41 placements carry 0xFF.

Sss.params_observed: kaze 0x00ffc800 x10, 0x00ffc8ff x12, 0x00ff4600 x4, 0x00ffffff x4; Cave08 0x00ff4600 x4; kindan 0x00ff3cff x5, 0x00ff5001 x2. So kaze uses range 2000 with both the 35-segment and 1-segment forms, and kindan's 0x...01 entries are the short form.
Sss.rot_scale: Placement rot is (0,0,0) in kaze and Cave08 and (0, 0x4000 = 90 degrees, 0) in kindan. The recovered create path builds its matrix from YrotS(current.angle.y) then XrotM(current.angle.x), so the placement rot sets the arm's rest orientation. Scale is 1.0 in all 41 placements and no setBaseScale was found - treat scale as unused. Health is initialised to 2 and a random phase offset is seeded with cM_rndF.
Sss.behaviour: A hostile plant claw that hangs from the ceiling: a procedurally drawn vine (1 or 35 segments) with the sss_hand model (arm plus three finger joints) at the tip and open/close animations. It idles until the player comes within 10*range units (or its switch fires), then extends and grabs. Three damage spheres of radius 20 along the body accept almost every attack type (everything except boomerang, water, wind and light), and a SEPARATE radius-80 sphere accepts only boomerang and wind - so the boomerang and the Deku Leaf gust have their own, much larger catch volume.
Sss.activates_on: player distance < 10 * ((params>>8)&0xFF) units, defaulting to 250 when that byte is 0xFF, or the optional switch in bits 16-23.
Sss.effect: grabs and attacks the player; can be cut, with the vine line reacting. Registered as fopAc_ENEMY_e, not as BG and not as a climbable.
Sss.implementation_note: Do NOT model this as a climbable rope. Draw the vine as a 1- or 35-segment line hanging from the anchor with the hand mesh at the tip, playing hiraku/tojiru for open/close. Aggro sphere radius = 10 * (params>>8 & 0xFF), default 250. Hit volumes: 3 spheres r=20 on the body for melee and arrows, 1 sphere r=80 for boomerang and Deku-Leaf wind. HP 2. Because the whole cpp is a stub, the exact motion curves, the grab hold and the cut sequence are NOT recoverable - approximate them or defer this actor until you have reference footage. This one probably belongs in enemies.json rather than a world-actor script.
